option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: anthro mutations
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded anthro animal mutation fangs bite teeth beast
option.helptext:
Adds this fork's animal-trait mutations to the physical mutation list - the ordinary animal end Qud has almost none of.
{{Y|Fangs}}, 3 points. A bite alongside whatever you are wielding, roughly one round in five. Your face slot stays free.
{{Y|Keen Smell}}, 3 points. Scent creatures at twice Heightened Hearing's range, but walls stop a smell dead.
{{Y|Tail}}, 1 point. 1 DV, and an Agility save against being knocked down.
Off hides them at character creation. Applies to a {{y|new}} character.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: graded burden
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded burden encumbrance weight carry capacity overburdened
option.helptext:
Makes carrying weight a gradient instead of a cliff.
Vanilla has one threshold - 15 pounds per point of Strength, then Overburdened, unable to move. Below it, nothing at all.
This puts three bands underneath. Lightly burdened at half capacity, -1 DV. Encumbered at three quarters, -2 DV. Heavily burdened at nine tenths, -4 DV, -10 Quickness, and no running.
Overburdened is untouched. Player only, and safe to toggle mid-run.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mutated Human mutation points
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation points mutant chargen
option.helptext:
How many mutation points a Mutated Human starts character creation with.
Vanilla Caves of Qud gives 12. Caves of Qud Expanded has always given 16, which is the default here.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} Changing it has no effect on a character that already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Mutated Human hit points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation hit points hp level mutant health
option.helptext:
How many hit points a Mutated Human rolls each level, applied from your next level onward.
{{G|1-5}} is this mod's: swingier than vanilla, with a higher ceiling. {{y|2-3}} is what version 2.2 shipped, apparently by mistake. {{y|1-4}} is vanilla's.
True Kin and Psionic Adepts are unaffected.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: extra skill points per level
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill points level gain mutant true kin
option.helptext:
Grants the extra skill points per level this mod has always given: {{G|65}} for a Mutated Human against vanilla's 50, and {{G|85}} for a True Kin against vanilla's 70.
Turn this off to earn exactly vanilla's. It applies from your next level and never takes back points you have earned. Psionic Adepts are unaffected.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: extra starting skills
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting skills chargen cooking staunch wounds

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: eased skill requirements
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill requirements attribute axe cudgel long blade multiweapon en garde

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: retuned skill point costs
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded skill point cost tinkering cooking butchery spicer reverse engineer
option.helptext:
Keeps this mod's skill point prices: {{W|Reverse Engineer}} {{G|200}}, and {{W|Butchery}} and {{W|Spicer}} {{G|100}} each.
The Cooking prices pay for the free skills {{W|extra starting skills}} grants, so if that is off you may want this off too. Applies immediately.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: starting reputation bonus
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting reputation joppa faction chargen

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: home base building in Joppa
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded joppa building home base becoming nook
option.helptext:
Adds a walled building near Argyve's workshop in Joppa: a bed, storage, an oven, and a becoming nook with a cybernetics rack.
{{y|Takes effect when you restart the game, and applies to Joppa as it is first generated.}} A character who already has the building keeps it, and one made without it will not gain it later - Joppa is built once, and what it was built with is in the save.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: don't offer artifacts you marked important
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded important marked artifact give argyve knickknack picker protect
option.helptext:
Keeps artifacts you marked {{Y|important}} out of the list when Argyve asks for a knickknack.
Vanilla offers him every artifact you carry, with no warning before a marked relic is gone. With this on, yours are simply not listed - and if they are all you have, you are told how to undo it rather than handed an empty menu.
Artifacts the {{y|game}} marked important are still offered, but ask you to confirm.
Applies immediately. Changes what a list shows, never what you own.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: ask a creature its name
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded ask name conversation npc creature introduce naming
option.helptext:
Adds {{G|What is your name?}} to conversations with creatures that have none yet, and they answer - drawn from their own culture, faction and region, in Caves of Qud's own wording.
{{y|Asking means you can no longer rename them.}} The game refuses to rename anyone who already has a name, so a creature that has told you who it is cannot be renamed by you afterwards. Turn this off if you would rather name your companions yourself.
Applies immediately. Names already given are kept.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Trash Divining runs dry as a zone is picked over
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded trash divining secrets rifle garbage scavenging density diminishing
option.helptext:
Makes a zone's trash run out of things to tell you, instead of paying the same rate for all hundred piles.
{{Y|Trash Divining}} rolls 5% per pile, and the catacombs lay down 80 to 100 of them in one zone. With this on the first twenty still pay {{Y|5%}} in full; after that the same zone drops to {{Y|3%}}, then {{Y|2%}}, then {{Y|1%}}, and no lower. Thin zones never reach the second band.
The count is per zone and keeps running while this is off.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: psionic chips in loot
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded psionic chip drops loot artifact tables
option.helptext:
Lets psionic chips and chipsets appear in the world, rolled from the artifact tables at tiers 3 through 8.
Turn this off for the mod's weapons, armor and genotypes without the chip economy - no chip can be tinkered, so this closes the supply. Applies immediately.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: True Kin Chip Interface slots
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface slot chargen psionic implant true kin
option.helptext:
Gives a True Kin the {{G|2}} Chip Interface slots this mod grants them. Psionic Adepts are unaffected - their {{G|4}} are the genotype. A Mutated Human has none either way: chips grant mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate, and that one can.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} A body is built once, at character creation, so this cannot change a character who already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Chip Interface slots on other humanoids
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface npc humanoid anatomy world
option.helptext:
Gives every other humanoid a Chip Interface slot, merged into the base humanoid anatomy. Nothing here puts a chip in an NPC's slot, so leaving it on has no effect you can see. Your own slots are the option above.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} Bodies are built once, when a creature is generated.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: how your own random name sounds
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded name random player character masc femme sound rename
option.helptext:
Chooses which pool your own name is drawn from when the game rolls one for you.
Masc gives the hard-stopped endings vanilla has always used, femme the open vowel-final ones, and random splits evenly between those and a mixed pool - which is what you get if you never touch this.
It does nothing if you type a name in. Renaming yourself in game draws from the same pool, so a change here takes effect on your next rename.
It does not touch anyone else in the world.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: choose your gender at character creation
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded gender chargen character creation pronoun nonbinary trans
option.helptext:
Adds a Gender row to character creation.
Qud ships thirteen genders with full grammar and no way to pick one, so the game rolls for you. This turns the row on and widens it from four to thirteen: elverson, xe, ze, sie, fae, spivak, ve, per and ne join male, female, neuterperson and nonspecific.
The hindren third gender is deliberately not offered. It is theirs.
Off hides the row and the game picks, as vanilla does. A character who has one keeps it.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: choose your pronouns at character creation
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded pronoun pronouns chargen character creation neopronoun they
option.helptext:
Adds a Pronoun Set row to character creation, separate from gender.
Qud tracks pronouns apart from gender, so you can take one gender's grammar and a different set of pronouns. The row defaults to {{y|from gender}}, which is what you want unless you want something else.
On, it offers fourteen sets - the three Qud already wrote and never showed anyone, plus one per gender.
Off hides the row and your pronouns follow your gender, as vanilla does.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: charmed merchants still expect paying
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded merchant charm beguile proselytize lovesick mask trade price free shop
option.helptext:
A merchant you have charmed still charges you for their goods.
Qud shares a companion's possessions with you and a charmed shopkeep counts as one, so beguiling or masking a trader empties their whole shop for free.
The charm is not weakened anywhere else - they still follow you, still fight for you, and their never-for-sale items stay on the shelf. A merchant who genuinely joined you is unaffected, because the test is the charm rather than the following.
Off makes the shop free again, from the next trade screen.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: arrows can be picked back up
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded arrow arrows bow archery ammo ammunition recover retrieve break
option.helptext:
An arrow you shoot sometimes survives and lands where it hit, so you can pick it up again.
How often depends on what it is made of - a wooden arrow about a fifth of the time, a zetachrome one about nine times in ten. So the arrows worth keeping are the ones you keep.
Arrows that carry something - explosive, cryo, gas, honey, flare - never come back. The payload is spent.
Off makes fired arrows vanish again, from the next shot.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: weapons wear from use
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded weapon wear durability broken repair tinkering
option.helptext:
How fast weapons wear out and eventually break. Armour already wears from being hit; this makes weapons wear from being used.
0 off, 1 light, 2 normal, 3 heavy. A weapon breaks after 19 points of wear and is repaired the same way broken armour is.
Higher-tier weapons wear far more slowly than low-tier ones.

option.DisplayText: Disease onsets say what is happening
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded disease glotrot ironshank monochrome onset warning
option.helptext:
A disease onset tells you it has begun, warns you on the fourth of its five days, and says when you have fought it off.
Vanilla only reports an onset once you have already failed a save, so an onset you beat outright can pass in complete silence.

option.DisplayText: Heavy blows leave wounds that rest will not close
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded wounds difficulty healing regeneration physic treatment
option.helptext:
A single blow taking half your hit points leaves a wound. Natural healing then stops a quarter short of full until it is treated.
Any treatment clears it - a bandage, salve, an injector, the Physic skills, a regeneration tank or a healing meal. Untreated it fades on its own.
Damage over time never wounds, and the Regeneration mutation shrinks the wound as it ranks up. Off by default: this makes the game harder.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: plainer relic names
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded relic name naming history spice plain register artifact
option.helptext:
Adds name forms for legendary relics built from plain words rather than exotic ones - {{y|the cold hatchet}} beside {{y|the sagittal quincunx}}.
Qud's relic vocabulary is large, so the trouble was never too few words. It is that nearly all of them are strange, and strangeness stops meaning anything with nothing ordinary beside it.
Vanilla's forms are never removed, so a plain name becomes {{y|likelier}} rather than a strange one impossible.
{{y|Takes effect when you restart the game.}} Relics that already have names keep them.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: creatures use what they pick up
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded creature npc equip pickup weapon reequip loot combat
option.helptext:
A creature that picks up a better weapon works out that it is better, instead of carrying it and going on swinging.
What it will work out depends on what it could plausibly understand. A tinker reconsiders anything, artifacts included. Everyone else reconsiders a stick with an edge, and leaves the guns alone.
Loadouts creatures already had are untouched - this only applies to something picked up after.
{{y|This makes fights harder.}} Off returns them to swinging what they started with, from the next pickup.
